Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Chicago/Romeoville, IL
619 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Increasing heat and humidity is expected next week with 
  periodic shower and storm chances.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 306 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

Surface high pressure continues to expand across the region 
early this morning in the wake of yesterday's cold front. This
will lead to a period of largely quiescent weather through the 
end of the week. A lake breeze is expected to push inland today 
which may provide enough lift for a few spotty showers or 
sprinkles as a weak disturbance moves across the area (15% 
chance). Coverage should remain very isolated if they even
develop given limited moisture availability and shallow cloud 
depths. Otherwise rain-free weather is in store across the area
through at least Saturday afternoon with highs in the upper 70s
to lower 80s and comfortable humidity.

Mostly clear skies early this morning and again tonight may 
allow for sufficient radiational cooling for shallow patchy fog 
development, particularly along river valleys and typical fog 
prone low spots outside of Chicago.

Looking ahead, the upper level pattern begins to transition 
toward upper ridging building across the central CONUS with 
multiple waves expected to traverse the Northern Plains and 
Upper Midwest this weekend through much of the upcoming week. 
The first of these waves may arrive as early as Saturday 
night in the form of a decaying convective complex. Latest 
guidance suggests that if this convection forms upstream it 
would likely be outrunning the unstable airmass with southeast
extent and residual low-level dry air across the area would 
likely limit the coverage of lightning or any potential severe 
weather here locally.

The degree of heating as well as our shower and thunderstorm 
chances for much of the upcoming week will be dependent upon the
strength of the aforementioned upper ridge. A stronger ridge 
would result in warmer (potentially highs in the 90s) and more 
humid conditions with the focus for greater thunderstorm 
coverage ending up north of the area. In contrast, a weaker 
upper ridge would support warmer conditions but to a lesser 
degree (mid-upper 80s) paired with frequent rounds of showers 
and thunderstorms. Suspect we may end up somewhere in between 
these two scenarios and will continue to refine the details as 
it gets closer. Stay tuned.

Petr

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 18Z FRIDAY/...
Issued at 619 AM CDT Thu Aug 27 2026

Forecast concerns for the terminals...

- Lake breeze to result in easterly winds at the Chicago
  terminals and GYY this afternoon. 

- Period of patchy fog expected tonight away from Chicago, IFR
  visibilities possible. 


A surface high continues to build into the region this morning
which will keep dry and generally tranquil weather around for
this TAF period. While there remains a low chance (10-15%) for 
an isolated shower or sprinkle along the lake breeze this 
afternoon, confidence on coverage remains too low for a formal
TAF mention but did keep a BKN050 mention going at ORD, MDW, and
GYY to tease this potential. Expect winds to remain northwesterly
through the afternoon at DPA and RFD with speeds around 5-7 
kts. A lake breeze will move through the Chicago terminals and 
GYY, however, which will result in an easterly wind shift and 
uptick in speeds to around 10 kts. Overall lake breeze timing 
continues to favor around 19-20z for MDW and ORD respectively 
and 16-17z at GYY, but will obviously keep a close eye on trends
in case that timing shifts.

Winds will gradually become light and variable overnight as the
center of the surface high passes overhead before settling into
a southwesterly direction Friday morning. Given the light winds
and clear skies forecast tonight, conditions look favorable for
patchy fog to develop after midnight and persist through 
daybreak Friday morning away from the urban core of Chicago. 
With such a strong signal in guidance and the fact that shallow 
fog has developed in spots the past couple nights, have opted to
introduce TEMPO groups at DPA, RFD, and GYY for MVFR visibilities
and fog. Though, there is a chance that visibilities could dip 
into the IFR range in spots. Aside from the fog, VFR conditions 
are expected through the TAF period. 

Yack

&&

.LOT WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IL...None.
IN...None.
LM...None.
